newsitem.title: CHINA: Jiangling aims to issue new B shares.
newsitem.headline: Jiangling aims to issue new B shares.

text.p: China's Jiangling Motors Corp plans to launch an offer of an additional 170 million foreign currency B shares later this year, company spokesman Xiong Zhongping said on Wednesday.

Jiangling is awaiting the final approval of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, the country's top securities authority, to go ahead with the issue, Xiong told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
The company plans to appoint Vickers Ballas as the international coordinator and Shenzhen J&A Securities as the domestic chief underwriter, Xiong said.
He declined to reveal the pricing of the issue but said the company would use the prices of its existing B shares as a gauge before launching the offer.
Jiangling's B shares closed at HK$3.30 last Friday.
Shenzhen's B share market will resume trading on Thursday after a holiday to mark the return of the former British colony of Hong Kong to China at midnight on June 30.

Jiangling, which mainly makes light trucks, plans to use the funds raised to finance its Transit-series project in partnership with Ford Motor Corp to produce light commercial vehicles including vans, Xiong said.
Jiangling will also use some of the money to pay debts and boost cash flow, Xiong said, adding that the issue would help reduce Jiangling's financing costs.

Ford, which has a 20 percent equity stake in Jiangling by holding B shares, has said it planned to lift its total stake in the firm to about 30 percent by purchasing 120 million of the new B shares for US$54.5 million.
After the deal, Ford would hold 258.64 million Jiangling B shares, and remain the company's second largest shareholder, Jiangling has said.
Jiangling posted a net profit of 34.62 million yuan for 1996 against 3.95 million yuan in 1995 based on international accounting standards.
But sales fell to 1.69 billion yuan last year from 1.97 billion yuan in 1995 under Chinese accounting standards.

The Shenzhen-based Securities Times on Saturday quoted Jiangling chairman Sun Min as saying Jiangling has targeted profit of 60 million yuan on sales of two billion yuan for 1997. But the newspaper did not say whether the profit figure was before or after taxation.
Xiong declined to comment on the forecasts.
